processing: Ordinary Longjing method, pan-fired and pressed flat; the name refers to the picking time, not to a different process.
harvest_season: After Qingming (around 4 to 6 April) and before Guyu (around 20 April).
appearance_dry: Flat, green leaves, longer and somewhat broader than a pre-Qingming pick.
appearance_liquor: Clear yellow-green, a little deeper than a pre-Qingming lot.
appearance_wet: Larger green leaves, commonly with two or three leaves to the bud in lower grades.
taste_profile: Fuller and more robust than pre-Qingming Longjing, with a stronger toasted bean note and more body.

brewing.notes: It can take a little more heat than a pre-Qingming tea, but too much brings out bitterness; a bit less leaf is an easy fix.

vintage_note: Sold only as a harvest of the current year, in the second half of April and after. It costs less than Mingqian tea from the same place and is the everyday Longjing for many drinkers. Drink within a year, as its fresh edge fades.
description:
Yuqian Longjing is not a place or a cultivar but a timestamp. 'Yuqian' means 'before the rains', and it marks Longjing picked after Qingming but before Guyu, the solar term of grain rain, around 20 April.

By then the plants are growing fast, so the leaf is larger and longer than in the prized pre-Qingming pick. The making is the same pressing in a hot wok, but there is more material in the leaf to work with, and the tea reflects it.

That gives a fuller cup: more bean and toast, more body, and less of the tender floral quality of the earliest pick. Some drinkers prefer it for exactly that. Water just over 80 C suits it, and a lighter hand with the leaf heads off bitterness.

It is a seasonal term rather than a guarantee of quality: grades vary widely, and a top Yuqian can beat a mediocre Mingqian. Check the origin zone as well as the term, since the label can apply to Longjing from any of the three zones.
history: The term follows the traditional solar calendar, which Chinese tea growers use to rank spring pickings, and it is not tied to any one maker or date of invention. In the modern market it stands as the second step down from Mingqian in the Longjing price ladder and is usually pitched as the better value.
